validation.summary_requirements: Exactly the SUMMARY_SCHEMA keys; title, access, and pedagogy are nonempty strings; topics, key_results, and chapter_map are nonempty arrays; figures, image_candidates, and gems are arrays; image_candidates has at most 8 entries.
validation.title_check: Each summary title is nonempty and contains its scope title, or is contained by its scope title, allowing an edition qualifier while preserving source identity.
validation.access_check: Each summary access is nonempty and begins with the corresponding scope access value, case-insensitively; all scopes declare full access.
validation.shard_check: Expected read filenames are crosswalked per source because several source tags intentionally use compact read prefixes.
validation.cache_check: Every non-sidecar file directly under research/texts must have <filename>.meta.yaml, and every .meta.yaml must have its payload.
validation.image_check: Every image_candidates[].capture path in all read and summary JSON files must resolve to an existing file.

Full MIT-published course corpus read from the official MIT OpenCourseWare course site and downloadable package: posted lecture notes for Lectures 2–13 and 15–22; Problem Sets 1–11 with solutions; Fall 2005 background, midterm, and final exams with solutions; and both projects with supporting MAT, WAV, and MATLAB files. Lectures 1 (Course Overview), 14 (Gene Frantz guest lecture), and 23 (Caruso’s Orchestra) are listed in the schedule but have no posted note PDFs, so no content beyond their titles is inferred. The separately published required textbook was not treated as part of the open corpus. MIT OCW marks the course CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 except where otherwise noted; separately credited third-party material may have different rights.

Full book read from the complete, author-hosted 447-page PDF at https://user.it.uu.se/~pst23965/SAS-new.pdf, linked as “AVAILABLE FOR DOWNLOAD” from Petre Stoica’s official Uppsala University publications page. Coverage includes front matter; Chapters 1–6; Appendices A–D; bibliography; subject-grouped references; and index. Direct, layout-preserving ranged text extracts for all four chapter-boundary shards are cached locally with sidecars. The PDF retains Prentice Hall copyright and states all rights reserved, so legal reading access does not imply redistribution or adaptation rights.

The source identifies Julius O. Smith III, W3K Publishing, 2011, ISBN 978-0-9745607-3-1; maintained pages display a 2026-06-10 copyright footer. Copyright is retained and no broad reuse licence is stated. Compact local caches and metadata sidecars are stored as jos-s1 through jos-s4 under content/courses/digital-signal-processing/research/texts/.
